podcast.body: Credited to Wings, this song marked another instance where Paul McCartney repeated a year-end number one, following his success with The Beatles. "McCartney himself repeated on 1976's silly love songs, but that was credited to Wings."

podcast.body: This 1976 single by Wings became Paul McCartney's biggest hit with the band, spending five weeks at number one in the summer of 1976 and being named Billboard's top hit of the year. The song was explicitly directed at both his critics and John Lennon, addressing the criticism of his "easy-listening hits" and asserting the popularity of his "light pop" style. "Accordingly, Silly Love Songs was Wings' biggest hit of all, five weeks at number one in the summer of 76, and Billboard named it the year's top hit."
